title: NovusBridge pilot - throttle & caching economics sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on measured tokens/sec/$, the impact of prefix caching and KV cache hit rates, and batching tradeoffs. SE walked through recent benchmark runs, proposed throttle and autoscale tweaks to improve cost-efficiency while meeting 95th p99 latency targets. Customer asked about private VPC implications, audit logs, and next steps for an end-to-end run with their production traffic shape.
transcript:
Header: NovusBridge pilot - throttle & caching economics sync
Date: 2026-11-05 16:00 PT | Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Hannah (CSM), Maya (NovusBridge Head of ML), Jon (Platform), Elena (Security), Priya (SRE)

-- Auto-summary (may be incomplete) --
Diego: ran three runs with v2-compat quantized model, measured tokens per dollar improvements with prefix cache at 28% hit-rate in their workload; batching gave per-token savings but added tail latency; suggested lowering max-batch to 8 and enabling adaptive batching.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to go over the latest numbers from the lab runs and align on next steps for the production-shaped run.
[00:18] Maya: yep, thanks. we ran the 10k sample through our ingestion yesterday, curious about the cache numbers.
[00:27] Diego: cool, so quick context — we did three configs: baseline no-cache, prefix cache only, prefix + KV cache. used the quantized int8 v2 variant you gave us. sequences avg 420 tokens, 95th ~980.
[00:40] Jon: small note, our real traffic has a bimodal length, a lot sub-100 token plus the long long summaries.
[00:48] Diego: yeah that shows up, and it influences batching efficiency. baseline tokens/sec per dollar was about 5.6k tokens / $1 for your mix. with prefix cache at ~28% effectiveness we saw 17% improvement to 6.5k tokens / $1. with KV cache on top, hit-rate ~12% additional, ended up ~7.2k tokens / $1.
[01:12] Maya: so total about 28% better from both caches combined? that's pretty decent.
[01:16] Diego: roughly, though hit-rates vary by route. the long-tail sessions get less benefit from prefix cache but KV helps across turns.
[01:27] Elena: quick security Q — when you say KV cache, is any customer PII stored in it? and how's it encrypted / audited?
[01:36] Diego: good q. our default POC setup used ephemeral in-memory KV on the node; we do not persist to disk. for Private or Dedicated you can hook into your KMS and we use envelope encryption at rest + audit logs. I'll drop the security note in the notes link.
[01:54] Priya: we need to see the audit log retention config, SOC2 controls, and whether HSM is required.
[02:01] Samira: noted, Elena and Priya — we'll attach the SOC2 + KMS/HSM doc and a sample audit_events.csv from a run.

[02:20] Diego: switching to batching — we tried max-batch sizes of 32, 16, 8 and an adaptive policy that caps at latency SLOs. at 32 the throughput is highest but p95 tail jumps: p95 ~420ms -> 680ms, p99 ~1.2s. at 8 batch p95 ~240ms, p99 ~480ms. tokens per dollar improved by 9-14% at larger batch sizes but tail latencies exceed your 95th target for interactive routes.
[03:05] Jon: our priority routes are interactive — search-style completions — those need p95 < 500ms ideally. the async background summarization can be higher latency.
[03:17] Diego: exactly. suggestion: route traffic by policy: interactive to smaller batch sizes and higher priority queue, background to large batches. Redwood can do smart routing at the per-route level — run two pools or one pool with tiered queues.
[03:33] Maya: cost-wise how much overhead for running two pools?
[03:36] Diego: if you reserve separate Dedicated pools, there's a fixed unit cost; but in Hosted you can use priority routing with weight-based autoscale to effectively separate without double-reserving. For now for POC we ran a single pool with per-route policy — it cost about 7% more than fully shared but met latency.
[03:56] Hannah: also remember KV cache leads to memory growth on nodes; you might need higher instance types for high hit-rate workloads. we noted that in run-3 we bumped node spec and saw a small increase in cost but net tokens/$ still improved.

[04:18] Maya: what's the recommended throttle or autoscale policy? we've seen occasional spikes and our current infra autoscaler is a bit slow.
[04:27] Diego: we prototyped a throttle policy — burst tokens/sec cap then quick fallback to a smaller model variant when queue depth rises. so 95th percentiles keep low latency. you can implement graceful degradation: for example keep full model but set fallback to a quantized int4 variant for overflow.
[04:46] Jon: curious about quality delta for int4 fallback — did you run evals?
[04:50] Diego: did small evals on 200 prompt set: mean sBLEU drop small on summaries (~1.2 BLEU points) but some hallucination edgecases increase. we recommend canary fallback + automated eval triggers so you don't silently degrade.
[05:12] Maya: ok that seems reasonable. about the tokens/sec/$ metric, can you share the raw numbers and the cost model? we want to reconcile with our internal accounting.
[05:22] Samira: yes — we uploaded the benchmark sheet: https://redwood.share/pilot-results-novus-11-05.xlsx — it's got run params, node types, batch configs, cache hit-rate breakdown and cost calc.
[05:36] Priya: I'll pull that after call. For the production-shaped run, can you match our ingress spike profile? we have 600 rps 5-min spikes.
[05:46] Diego: we can run a trace-driven replay, yes. needs your anonymized traffic trace; we'll run two runs: baseline and optimized policy. estimate 6 hours of cluster time.
[05:59] Jon: timeline — when can we do that?
[06:02] Samira: earliest Thursday, but need trace and your auth for the test cluster. we can also spin up in your VPC for a private run if you prefer.

[06:20] Elena: security again — if we spin in our VPC, what's the onboarding lead time? and what about audit of ingress data?
[06:29] Samira: Private deployment onboarding is typically 2-3 weeks for full connectivity and KMS integration; for a temporary VPC peered test we can do a constrained run in 3-4 days. we'll surface the exact checklist.
[06:43] Diego: on caching knobs: prefix cache TTLs matter a lot. in run-2 we used 10-minute TTL, run-3 used 2-minute TTL and saw different hit-rates; for chat-heavy routes shorter TTL preserves freshness but reduces benefit.
[07:00] Maya: our conversations are high-sensitivity and we prefer shorter TTLs. but we want better tokens/$ too. any ideas?
[07:07] Diego: you can use selective caching by route and by intent classification: cache FAQs for longer TTLs, ephemeral session text for short. also row-level redaction before caching if PII present.
[07:22] Priya: can Redwood redact before cache write in the POC? we'd prefer that.
[07:26] Diego: yes, you can push a preprocessor hook in the pipeline to scrub tokens before writing to KV. we'll include a sample lambda for that.

[07:40] Samira: okay last block — cost tradeoff recs: for interactive routes use max-batch 8, adaptive auto-cap with latency SLO 500ms, prefix cache enabled with 2min TTL, no KV on those routes; background jobs: max-batch 32, enable KV with 10min TTL; fallback policy to int4 variant for overload; run production-shaped stress replay to validate 600rps spikes.
[08:10] Maya: good. can you also give a rough monthly cost delta if we move to Dedicated for the interactive pool?
[08:15] Diego: rough napkin: if your sustained peak needs 12x T4-equivalent nodes we'd estimate $Xk/mo dedicated vs $Yk hosted; net per-token cost might drop 8-12% but committed license and egress differences apply. we'll put the actual numbers in the spreadsheet.
[08:33] Jon: please include the sensitivity table — tokens/$ vs batch size and cache hit-rate.
[08:38] Diego: done in sheet.

[08:45] Elena: final compliance ask — can we get the data flow diagram and a sample incident response runbook?
[08:51] Hannah: we'll attach both; also include the SOC2 scoping note.

[09:00] Samira: recap quick: 1) Diego to run trace-driven production-shaped replay (baseline + optimized) once NovusBridge shares trace and test credentials; 2) Samira/Hannah to share SOC2/KMS/HSM + audit log example + redaction lambda; 3) Diego to add canary fallback config and int4 eval notes to the sheet; 4) schedule follow-up to review replay results and pick pilot cutover date.
[09:28] Maya: that works. can we aim to have the replay by Friday?
[09:32] Samira: we'll try for Friday EOD but at latest next Monday.

[09:40] Jon: thanks all.
[09:42] Meeting end.
